entries.title_tex: A: the dagger Bergner model structure
entries.statement_tex:
There is a left proper combinatorial model structure $\sCat^{\dag}_{\Bergner}$ on $\sCat^{\dag}$ with the prescribed generating cofibrations $I_{\dag}$, generating trivial cofibrations $J_{\dag}$, and dagger DK-equivalences $W_{\dag}$.
Its three classes are
\begin{align}
\mathrm{Cof}&=I_{\dag}\text{-}\cof,&
\mathrm{Fib}&=J_{\dag}\text{-}\inj,&
\mathrm{W}&=W_{\dag}.
\end{align}
Here $W_{\dag}$ consists of local weak homotopy equivalences that are essentially surjective up to coherently unitary equivalence, using the specified standard fibrant replacement.
The underlying category is locally finitely presentable, both generating families are small, and the domain of every generating map is finitely presentable.
A functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a trivial fibration if and only if it is surjective on objects and every map
$\mathcal C(x,y)\to\mathcal D(px,py)$ is a trivial Kan fibration.
entries.provenance_tex: Theorem A of Part I, including the model classes, generating data, trivial-fibration criterion, and left properness for the same model structure. The ordinary Kan--Quillen foundations are reused.

entries.title_tex: B: the dagger Joyal model and its Quillen equivalence
entries.provenance_tex: Theorem B of Part I. The comparison uses the original dagger lift of ordinary rigidification and the same standard dagger Joyal model appearing in the model-structure statement.

entries.title_tex: C: intrinsic recognition of dagger Joyal equivalences
entries.provenance_tex: Theorem C of Part I. The statement applies to every dagger morphism between dagger quasi-categories and relates local weak equivalences to unitary essential surjectivity.

entries.title_tex: D: the anti-involutive model and the comparison obstruction
entries.provenance_tex: Theorem D of Part I, together with the construction of the precise source model used in the formal statement. The obstruction concerns these specified models and adjunctions.

entries.title_tex: Presheaves on the reversal simplex category
entries.provenance_tex: The equivalence is constructed for the dagger simplicial sets of Part~I; it is not an existing Mathlib equivalence invoked under a new name.

entries.title_tex: Local finite presentability of dagger simplicial sets
entries.statement_tex:
For every universe $u$, the category $\sSet^{\dag}$ is locally finitely presentable at level $u$.
In particular, it is locally presentable.
entries.provenance_tex: The preceding project-specific presheaf equivalence transports Mathlib's presentability results for presheaf categories without changing the universe of values.

entries.title_tex: The free dagger simplicial-set adjunction
entries.provenance_tex: A left Kan extension along the ordinary-simplex inclusion into the reversal simplex category, transported through the presheaf equivalence, gives the original forgetful functor its left adjoint. The explicit pushout description is the separate result below.

entries.title_tex: Free completion as a pushout over the zeroth skeleton
entries.provenance_tex: The common vertices, both inclusions, the adjunction unit, and the dagger interchange equations are constructed together.

entries.title_tex: Images of monomorphisms under free completion
entries.statement_tex:
Let $\FdagSSet\dashv\UdagSSet$ be any chosen free--forgetful adjunction.
If $i:K\to L$ is a monomorphism of simplicial sets, then $\FdagSSet(i)$ is a free cofibration.
entries.provenance_tex: The proof uses the concrete pushout and positive-dimensional nondegenerate simplices. The conclusion concerns the specified free-cofibration predicate.

entries.title_tex: Free-boundary cell presentation of free cofibrations
entries.statement_tex:
Let $\FdagSSet\dashv\UdagSSet$ be any chosen free--forgetful adjunction, and let $I^{\sSet}_{\dag}$ be the family of free boundary inclusions $\FdagSSet(\partial\Delta^n)\to\FdagSSet(\Delta^n)$ in all degrees, as in Part~I.
Every free cofibration is a relative $I^{\sSet}_{\dag}$-cell complex.
As classes of morphisms,
\begin{align}
  I^{\sSet}_{\dag}\text{-}\cof
    &= \{f\mid f\text{ is a free cofibration}\}.
\end{align}
On the left, $I^{\sSet}_{\dag}\text{-}\cof$ is the closure of the free boundary inclusions under coproducts, pushouts, transfinite compositions, and retracts.
entries.provenance_tex: The relative skeletal filtration and its attaching pushouts give the cell presentation; individual closure lemmas are subsumed here.

entries.title_tex: Free cofibrations need not be normal monomorphisms
entries.statement_tex: In every universe $u$ there is a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of dagger simplicial sets that is a free cofibration, while its image among anti-involutive simplicial sets is not a normal monomorphism.
entries.provenance_tex: The counterexample uses the map from the initial object to the point object. It makes no general assertion about the cofibration classes of two model structures.

entries.title_tex: Ordinary equivalence need not be unitarily essentially surjective
entries.statement_tex: There are dagger categories $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ on small groupoids and a dagger-preserving functor $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ that is full, faithful, and an equivalence of ordinary categories, but is not essentially surjective by unitary isomorphisms.
entries.provenance_tex: A concrete two-object integer dagger groupoid supplies the example. The cited declaration does not include subsequent claims about nerves or weak equivalences.

entries.title_tex: Free dagger simplicial categories
entries.statement_tex:
For every universe $u$ and dagger simplicial graph $G$, there are a free dagger simplicial category $\FCatDag(G)$ and a graph map $\eta_G:G\to\UCatDag\FCatDag(G)$.
Restriction along $\eta_G$ classifies functors from $\FCatDag(G)$ to any dagger simplicial category by a bijection; hence $\FCatDag\dashv\UCatDag$.
entries.provenance_tex: The free category is built explicitly from finite paths and their simplicial mapping sets.

entries.title_tex: Monadicity over dagger simplicial graphs
entries.statement_tex: In a common universe $u$, the forgetful functor $\UCatDag$ from dagger simplicial categories to dagger simplicial graphs is a monadic right adjoint.
entries.provenance_tex: The free adjunction, reflection of isomorphisms, and graph-split coequalizers are established in the formalization before applying Mathlib's Beck theorem. This is distinct from forgetting to ordinary simplicial categories.

entries.title_tex: Dagger simplicial graphs as presheaves
entries.provenance_tex: The index category and equivalence encode endpoints, simplicial edges, and reversal. Presentability and completeness follow by transport from Mathlib's presheaf results.

entries.title_tex: Finitarity of the free-word monad
entries.statement_tex: In a common universe $u$ one may choose the free--forgetful adjunction $\FCatDag\dashv\UCatDag$ so that the composite $\UCatDag\FCatDag$ is $\aleph_0$-accessible.
entries.provenance_tex: The proof analyzes actual finite paths and endpoint pullbacks. It asserts finitarity for this particular monad, not for arbitrary monads.

entries.title_tex: Local finite presentability of dagger simplicial categories
entries.statement_tex:
In every common universe $u$, the category $\sCat^{\dag}$ has all $u$-small limits and colimits and is locally finitely presentable at level $u$.
In particular, it is locally presentable.
entries.provenance_tex: Colimits are constructed through semantic quotients of mapping spaces; finitely presentable free-graph generators then give the presentability criterion. This result does not assert a model structure.

entries.title_tex: Creation of limits and colimits by ordinary forgetting
entries.statement_tex:
Let $o$ and $v$ be independent universes for objects and simplicial mapping sets, and let $w,w'$ be independent universes for diagrams.
The functor $\UdagSCat:\sCat^{\dag}\to\sCat$ creates limits and colimits of size $(w',w)$, also when the object and mapping-set universes are respectively $o$ and $v$.
In particular, it lifts a given ordinary universal cone or cocone while retaining its apex.
entries.provenance_tex: This construction concerns forgetting to ordinary simplicial categories, rather than the monadic forgetful functor to dagger simplicial graphs.

entries.title_tex: Two-object free cells and finite presentability
entries.statement_tex:
For every universe $u$ and simplicial set $K$, there is a two-object free cell $\bbA_{\dag}(K)$ with objects $x,y$ and a specified map $K\to\bbA_{\dag}(K)(x,y)$.
Restriction along this data classifies maps from $\bbA_{\dag}(K)$ to any target dagger simplicial category by a bijection.
If, in addition, $K$ is a finite simplicial set, then $\bbA_{\dag}(K)$ is finitely presentable at level $u$.
entries.provenance_tex: The cell and its universal property are constructed directly; the finite-presentability conclusion uses Mathlib's result for finite simplicial sets under the stated extra hypothesis.

entries.title_tex: Small colimits of ordinary simplicial categories
entries.statement_tex: In a common universe $u$, the category $\sCat$ of ordinary simplicial categories has all $u$-small colimits.
entries.provenance_tex: The construction uses free paths and semantic quotients of simplicial mapping sets. It also supplies colimits needed for the ordinary rigidification below.

entries.title_tex: Ordinary rigidification, the coherent nerve, and opposites
entries.provenance_tex: The construction uses Mathlib's simplex thickening and presheaf Kan-extension API; the natural nerve and opposite comparisons, including coherence, are proved here. These are ordinary simplicial-categorical results.

entries.title_tex: Dagger rigidification and its adjunction
entries.provenance_tex: The dagger lift retains the full ordinary enriched mapping data. The adjunction alone does not assert a Quillen equivalence.

entries.title_tex: The Kan dagger core and the unitary core of a Kan object
entries.statement_tex:
Let $X$ be a dagger simplicial set in universe $u$.
If the underlying simplicial set of $X$ admits inner-horn fillers, then the underlying simplicial set of its original dagger core is a Kan complex, and its ordinary core $X^{\simeq}$ is the greatest Kan subcomplex of $X$.
If, in addition, the underlying simplicial set of $X$ is itself a Kan complex, there is an isomorphism
\begin{align}
  \calU(X)&\cong V_{\mathrm{can}}(X).
\end{align}
Here $\calU(X)$ is the unitary core of Part~I, and $V_{\mathrm{can}}(X)$ abbreviates Lean's \nolinkurl{canonicalVertexFunctor.obj X}.
entries.provenance_tex: The core construction and Kan property are established for the specified inner-horn hypothesis; the unitary-core isomorphism requires the additional Kan hypothesis.

entries.title_tex: Small object argument for finitely presentable domains
entries.statement_tex:
Let $C$ have object universe $u$ and Hom universe $v$.
Suppose that $C$ is locally small relative to an auxiliary universe $w$ and has the required small colimits of that size.
Let $I$ be a small family of morphisms whose domains are finitely presentable relative to $w$.
Then $I$ satisfies the small object argument relative to $w$.
In particular, no separate cardinal condition on individual generators is needed: the relative-cell colimit condition is verified at $\aleph_0$.
entries.provenance_tex: A general bridge proved in this formalization and applied to Mathlib's small object argument. The three universes and the smallness, colimit, and finite-presentability hypotheses remain explicit.

entries.title_tex: Boundary-cell presentations and lifting for simplicial sets
entries.statement_tex:
In any universe $u$, every monomorphism $i:X\to Y$ of ordinary simplicial sets admits a countable relative boundary-cell presentation that retains the original $X$, $Y$, and $i$.
Let $I$ be Mathlib's actual family of boundary inclusions in all degrees.
Then
\begin{align}
I\text{-}\cell
  &= \operatorname{Mono}(\sSet), \\
I^{\square} &= \operatorname{Mono}(\sSet)^{\square}
  \subseteq \operatorname{KanFib}(\sSet).
\end{align}
The final inclusion applies to maps with arbitrary source and target.
These conclusions alone do not identify boundary right lifting with weak homotopy equivalence or with trivial fibrations.
entries.provenance_tex: A boundary-cell construction and its lifting consequences proved here for ordinary simplicial sets, using Mathlib's boundary inclusions and Kan-fibration predicate.

entries.title_tex: Promotion of a local-presentability rank
entries.provenance_tex: A general proposition proved here using Mathlib's strong-generator criterion. Pullbacks and the regularity of both cardinals are retained as hypotheses.

entries.title_tex: Detection of weak equivalences by a localization
entries.provenance_tex: A general detection theorem proved here. It assumes an existing model structure and localization; it does not construct a Bousfield localization.

entries.title_tex: Local finite presentability of simplicial and bisimplicial sets
entries.provenance_tex: Concrete applications in this formalization of Mathlib's results on presheaf categories and strong generators. They supply ambient-category hypotheses for the small object and Smith constructions.

entries.title_tex: Functorial factorizations for the specified generators
entries.statement_tex:
In the category $\sCat^{\dag}$ with common universe $u$, let $I_{\dag}$ be the original union of boundary generators and the object generator.
Every morphism factors functorially with left leg in ${}^{\square}((I_{\dag})^{\square})$ and right leg in $(I_{\dag})^{\square}$.
Moreover, fix an object type $O$ in universe $u$.
For each of the original generating families $I_O$ and $J_O$ in $\sCat^{\dag}_O$, every morphism $f$ has functorial factorizations
\begin{align}
f &= r_I(f)\circ\ell_I(f),
  &\ell_I(f)&\in{}^{\square}(I_O^{\square}),
  &r_I(f)&\in I_O^{\square}, \\
f &= r_J(f)\circ\ell_J(f),
  &\ell_J(f)&\in{}^{\square}(J_O^{\square}),
  &r_J(f)&\in J_O^{\square}.
\end{align}
entries.provenance_tex: Concrete applications of the general small object argument after finite presentability is proved for the relevant domains. These factorizations alone do not identify a weak-equivalence class or establish a model structure.

entries.title_tex: A model structure on fixed-object strict dagger groupoids
entries.statement_tex:
Fix a type $O$ in universe $u$.
Let $\sGpd^{\dag}_O$ be the full subcategory of $\sCat^{\dag}_O$ spanned by the objects satisfying the original degreewise invertibility condition; its morphisms are dagger-preserving functors whose object map is the identity on $O$.
This category has a model structure.
For a morphism $F:C\to D$, weak equivalences and fibrations are detected on every Hom map $F_{x,y}$, for $x,y\in O$:
\begin{align}
F\in W
  &\Longleftrightarrow
    \forall x,y\in O,\;F_{x,y}\in W_{\sSet}, \\
F\in\Fib
  &\Longleftrightarrow
    \forall x,y\in O,\;F_{x,y}\in\Fib_{\sSet}.
\end{align}
Cofibrations are the left lifting class of the specified trivial fibrations in this category.
entries.provenance_tex: A concrete model structure established here after the required factorizations are proved. The fixed-object category retains the original dagger enrichment and strictness. This theorem does not establish the simplicial model axioms or all of Theorem C.

entries.title_tex: Generation of normal monomorphisms by boundaries in all degrees
entries.provenance_tex: A concrete generation theorem proved here with the original normality predicate and free boundary maps in all degrees, rather than a positive-degree substitute.

entries.title_tex: Construction of the ordinary Joyal model structure
entries.provenance_tex: A concrete Smith application assembled here for ordinary simplicial sets, not a new proof of a general Smith recognition theorem. It supplies the ordinary model used in the next comparison.

entries.title_tex: The anti-involutive Joyal model and its right-induced classes
entries.provenance_tex: A concrete Smith application in the anti-involutive category and an identification of right-induced weak equivalences and fibrations relative to the constructed ordinary Joyal model. This is the existence component of the model used in Theorem D.

entries.title_tex: A Kan--Quillen self-equivalence from $Q_{\mathrm{rc}}$
entries.statement_tex:
In every universe $u$, the left Kan extension
$\operatorname{Real}_{Q_{\mathrm{rc}}}:\sSet\to\sSet$ of the original
right-cone cosimplicial object $Q_{\mathrm{rc}}$ and its right adjoint
$\operatorname{Sing}_{Q_{\mathrm{rc}}}$ form a Quillen equivalence for the
ordinary Kan model structure.
In particular, for every Kan complex $X$, the counit
$\operatorname{Real}_{Q_{\mathrm{rc}}}\operatorname{Sing}_{Q_{\mathrm{rc}}}X\to X$
is a weak equivalence.
This is not the adjunction between topological realization and the ordinary
singular complex of a topological space.
entries.provenance_tex: The construction and comparison for the original right-cone object $Q_{\mathrm{rc}}$ are proved in this formalization, using the existing Kan model structure and Mathlib's Quillen-equivalence criterion. This is an ordinary simplicial-set result, distinct from the dagger rigidification result in Theorem B.

entries.title_tex: The projective model structure on simplicial $C_2$-actions
entries.statement_tex:
In every universe $u$, the category
$\Fun(BC_2,\sSet)_{\proj}$ of simplicial $C_2$-actions admits a projective
model structure.
If $U$ is the forgetful functor and $f$ is an equivariant map, then
\begin{align}
 f\text{ is a weak equivalence}&\iff U(f)\text{ is a Kan weak equivalence},\\
 f\text{ is a fibration}&\iff U(f)\text{ is a Kan fibration}.
\end{align}
Its cofibrations form the left lifting class generated by the free simplicial
boundary inclusions.
The assertion concerns this $C_2$-action category; it does not claim the same
construction unconditionally for every group.
entries.provenance_tex: The free-boundary and free-horn generators, finite-source smallness, and closure of weak equivalences are verified for this action category. The construction uses Mathlib, the ported TopPackage machinery, and the ordinary Kan model structure; it does not present that general machinery as a new theorem.

entries.title_tex: The Borel model structure on topological $C_2$-actions
entries.statement_tex:
In every universe $u$, the category of $C_2$-actions in
$\mathrm{TopCat}$ admits a Borel model structure.
An equivariant map is a weak equivalence, respectively a fibration, exactly
when its underlying map has that property in the existing
$\mathrm{TopCat}$ model structure.
The cofibrations coincide with the original Borel left lifting class.
The result uses that particular topological model structure and makes no claim
about a different category of topological spaces.
entries.provenance_tex: This is a concrete model construction for the action category, using free realized boundaries and horns and finite free realization sources. The underlying topological q-model and package machinery are reused from pinned TopCatModelCategory sources; their upstream proofs are not claimed as new independent proofs here.

entries.title_tex: Cofibrancy of $E_{\bullet}C_2$ and contractibility of $EC_2$
entries.statement_tex:
In every universe $u$, the $C_2$-action on the simplicial set
$E_{\bullet}C_2$ is cofibrant in the projective model structure above.
Its topological realization $EC_2:=|E_{\bullet}C_2|$ is contractible as an
\emph{underlying} topological space.
Thus the two conclusions are $\operatorname{IsCofibrant}(E_{\bullet}C_2)$ and
$\operatorname{ContractibleSpace}(EC_2)$.
The first follows from an equivariant relative cell complex built from free
boundary cells; the second follows by realizing an explicit contraction.
The latter does not assert equivariant contractibility or contractibility of
fixed-point spaces.
entries.provenance_tex: The action, skeletal pushouts, equivariant relative cell complex, and simplicial contraction are constructed for the original $E_{\bullet}C_2$. General cell-complex and topological-realization APIs are reused from Mathlib and TopCat.

entries.title_tex: Kan fibers of prefix mapping spaces
entries.statement_tex:
Let $X\in\sSet$ be a quasi-category in any universe $u$.
For every $k\geq0$, every $k$-simplex $\sigma$ of $X$, and every vertex $b$,
the fiber $\operatorname{prefixMapping}(X,\sigma,b)$ of the original coslice
projection over $b$ is a Kan complex.
The case $k=0$ includes the Kan property of the ordinary left mapping space.
The stated result retains the quasi-category hypothesis on $X$.
entries.provenance_tex: The proof uses lifting for the original coslice projection and the Kan criterion for its fibers. The statement covers every prefix simplex and terminal vertex, rather than an individual simplicial face calculation.

entries.title_tex: Weak-equivalence invariance of right mapping spaces
entries.statement_tex:
Let $X,Y$ be quasi-categories in any universe $u$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
categorical weak equivalence, and let $a,b\in X_0$.
The induced map of the original right-cone mapping spaces
\begin{align}
 \Map^{R}_{X}(a,b)
  &\to \Map^{R}_{Y}(f(a),f(b))
\end{align}
is a weak equivalence of ordinary simplicial sets.
No monomorphism or Kan-fibration assumption is imposed on $f$.
entries.provenance_tex: The proof uses the original right-cone mapping spaces, a span for categorical weak equivalences, and lifting. It is distinct from the unitary-core criterion in the dagger Theorem C.

entries.title_tex: Right-cone mapping spaces and $Q_{\mathrm{rc}}$-singular enriched Homs
entries.statement_tex:
Let $D\in\sCat$ be an ordinary simplicial category in any universe $u$,
and let $v,w$ be vertices of its coherent nerve.
Write $\bar v,\bar w$ for their corresponding objects of $D$.
There is an isomorphism of simplicial sets
\begin{align}
 \operatorname{rightConeSimplices}_{D}(v,w)
  &\cong \operatorname{Sing}_{Q_{\mathrm{rc}}}(D(\bar v,\bar w)).
\end{align}
The comparison is bijective in every simplicial degree and respects the
simplicial operators.
No additional naturality statement in $D,v,w$ is asserted here.
entries.provenance_tex: The isomorphism compares the original cone evaluation with the original $Q_{\mathrm{rc}}$-singular construction. It concerns mapping objects and is separate from the ordinary rigidification--coherent-nerve adjunction itself.

reused_foundations.provenance: Pinned TopCatModelCategory compatibility port; reused upstream proofs.
